summary: John Clifford Holt is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Gustavus Adolphus College, Graduate Theological Union, and the University of Chicago under Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah, he served as Professor of Religion at Bowdoin College (1978–2019).
John Cockburn Thomson was an Indologist. He earned his B.A. from Trinity College, Oxford (1852–1857), studying under Horace Hayman Wilson and Christian Lassen.

John Collinson Nesfield worked in linguistics and Indology. Educated at Highgate School and Merton College, he taught at Highgate School (1859–1864), Presidency University (~1867–1872), Krishnagar Government College (~1872–1874), and served as principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1878).
John Correia-Afonso was a historian and archaeologist. He studied under Henry Heras (~1950–1953) and later succeeded him.

John Corrigan is a religious studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Chicago (~1976–1982). He held appointments at the University of Virginia, Arizona State University, and Florida State University, where he chaired the religion department around 2001.

John Crawfurd was a linguist, historian, and archaeologist. After completing his M.D. at the University of Edinburgh (~1800–1803), he served as a physician for the East India Company (1803–1808) and succeeded Stamford Raffles in 1823.
John Cripps Pembrey was an Indologist and linguist who served as Oriental Reader at Clarendon Press, attested in 1904 and 1916.
John Cumming was an Indologist and historian. He earned degrees from the University of Glasgow and Balliol College, Oxford, and served as Vice-Chairman at SOAS University of London from 1925 to 1946.
John D'Oyly was an Indologist and linguist. He was educated at Corpus Christi College and the University of Cambridge, earning his B.A. between 1792 and 1796.

John D. Dunne specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. Educated at Amherst College and Harvard University under supervisors including Masatoshi Nagatomi and Malcolm David Eckel, he held faculty posts at Emory University (~2005–2016) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (from 1999).

John D. Kelly is an Indologist, historian, and archaeologist who held posts at the University of Chicago, where he was Christian W. Mackauer Professor of Anthropology and Social Sciences (attested 2007, 2026).

John D. Smith is an Indologist and linguist. He served as Lecturer in Sanskrit at SOAS University of London (1975) and taught at the University of Cambridge as University Lecturer in Sanskrit (1984) and Professor (2001–2007).

John Daido Loori was a Buddhist studies figure. He studied at Rutgers University and trained under Soen Nakagawa and Taizan Maezumi, whom he succeeded. He served as Abbot of Zen Mountain Monastery (~1980–2009) and founded the Mountains and Rivers Order.
John Daishin Buksbazen is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the Zen Center of Los Angeles under Taizan Maezumi and Bernie Glassman (attested 2002).
John David Paterson was an Indologist and historian who founded The Asiatic Society. He joined the East India Company in 1776 and served as a Judge and Magistrate at the University of Dhaka.

John David Rees was an Indologist educated at Cheltenham College. He served in the Madras Civil Service (from 1875), the Indian Civil Service (~1875–1901), and as an Additional Member of the Council of India (1895–1900).

John Dawson Mayne was an Indologist who studied at Trinity College Dublin (~1845–1849). He served as Professor of Law at Presidency College, Chennai (~1857–1872) and Professor of Common Law at the Inns of Court (1880–1885).

John DeFrancis was a sinologist and linguist who studied at Yale University (~1937–1941) and Columbia University (~1941–1946). He held posts at Seton Hall University (~1961–1966) and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~1966–1976).

John Dewey was a philosopher educated at the University of Vermont (~1875–1879) and Johns Hopkins University (~1882–1884). He held posts at the universities of Michigan, Minnesota, Chicago (~1894–1904), and Columbia University (~1904–1930).

John Dowson was an Indologist, linguist, and historian who studied under Edwin Norris. He served as Tutor at the East India Company College (~1855–1858) and Professor of Hindustani at University College London and Staff College, Camberley (1855–1877).
